title: The Integration Boost is computed from per-block USDS balances in the partner venue against the Sky Savings Rate
content:
Each Integration Boost Instance carries a "Savings Rate Adjustment Strategy" parameter with the same construction (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.2.1.1.7 for Euler, .2.1.7 for Curve, .3.1.7 for Morpho): "The Integration Boost is calculated based on **per block values for USDS in [the venue] and the Sky Savings Rate**."

Two design choices are packed into that sentence. Measurement is **per block**, so the boost tracks the integral of USDS held in the venue over time rather than a snapshot — a partner cannot earn by staging a large balance on a measurement date, and cannot lose the whole period's accrual to a momentary outflow.

And the benchmark is the **Sky Savings Rate**, the return USDS holders get for simply saving in Sky. Naming the SSR in the formula makes the boost a *spread over the alternative*: the boost's job is to make holding USDS inside Euler, Curve or Morpho competitive with holding it in Sky's own savings product. The primitive is titled a "Savings Rate Adjustment Strategy" precisely because that is what it is.

The consequences are real. The cost of an integration is not fixed — it scales with the partner's success, so a wildly successful integration is proportionally expensive. And because the boost is indexed to the SSR, a change in Sky's own savings rate mechanically changes what Skybase pays every integration partner, coupling this Agent's spending to a Stability Scope parameter it does not control.
description: Boost accrues continuously from how much USDS sits in the integration, benchmarked to the SSR — making it a rate spread over the base savings rate rather than a flat integration fee.
